reviews.reason: Printed p114 begins this unit with በ followed by raised apparatus number 29, not an asterisk. The asterisk before ዓዚዛን is printed. The speakers introduced here are the condemned mighty and kings; their subsequent praise belongs to their plea for respite. The English is substantially defensible, but all three note attachments need correction.
reviews.suggested_text: In those days the mighty ones and the kings who possess the dry land[a] will beg the angels of punishment, into whose custody they have been delivered[b], to give them a little respite[c], so that they may fall down and worship before the Lord of Spirits and confess their sins before him.
reviews.footnote_changes: Attach a to 'dry land,' b to the custody clause, and c to 'a little respite.' Do not present the custody construction as more certain than its existing textual qualification allows.
reviews.suggested_source_text: በእማንቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ያስተበቍዑ፡ *ዓዚዛን፡ ወነገሥት፡ እለ፡ ይእኅዝዋ፡ ለየብስ፡ እመላእክት፡ መቅሠፍት፡ በኀበ፡ ሀለዉ፡ ምጥዋነ፡ ከመ፡ የሀቦሙ፡ ዕረፍተ፡ ንስቲተ፡ ከመ፡ ይደቁ፡ ወይስግዱ፡ በቅድመ፡ እግዚአ፡ መናፍስት፡ ወይትአመኑ፡ ኃጢአቶሙ፡ በቅድሜሁ።

reviews.reason: The unit crosses p114–115. Blessing and praising are both present here, unlike the shining verb in verse 3. The repeated titles and printed asterisks should remain distinct from raised apparatus numbers. The principal English wording is acceptable; note c merely repeats it.
reviews.suggested_text: And they will bless and praise the Lord of Spirits and say, “Blessed is the Lord of Spirits, the Lord of kings, the Lord of the mighty, the Lord of the rich, the Lord of glory, and the Lord of wisdom.”
reviews.footnote_changes: Delete redundant note c. Attach the wealth alternative to 'rich.' If retaining the repetition note, attach it to the title sequence rather than the opening occurrence of 'Lord of Spirits.'

reviews.reason: Printed p115 reads ወይበርህ, a shining/light verb, not a blessing verb. Neither 'is blessed' nor the previous-rendering note preserves this distinction. The remainder concerns unfathomable, innumerable hidden things and righteousness beyond reckoning.
reviews.suggested_text: And your power shines in every hidden thing, from generation to generation, and your glory forever and ever. Deep are all your hidden things, and they are without number; your righteousness is beyond reckoning.
reviews.footnote_changes: Remove note c's blessing alternative. Attach the mysteries alternative to 'hidden things' and the justice alternative to 'righteousness,' not to unrelated clauses.

reviews.reason: The rulers continue speaking. The source supports their present recognition and dependent praise/blessing clause. 'Ought to' is an interpretive modal rendering, not an independently expressed obligation; the existing alternative appropriately acknowledges this. The main defect is note attachment.
reviews.suggested_text: Now we know that we ought to praise and bless[a] the Lord of kings[b] and the one who reigns over all kings.
reviews.footnote_changes: Move a to the praise/blessing clause. Keep b with 'Lord of kings.' Do not describe the hortatory alternative as a different printed reading.

reviews.reason: P115 apparatus 24 explicitly directs that the introductory verb be taken as future here; 'they said' disregards that instruction. 'Believe' also obscures the confessional sense available in this lament. The exact English force of the following question or wish for respite should remain held rather than silently changing a past-form expression into an uncomplicated future question.
reviews.suggested_text: Bounded repair: “And they will say, … so that we may praise him, thank him, and confess before your glory.” The intervening request or wish for respite remains unresolved.
reviews.footnote_changes: Attach the respite note to 'rest/respite.' Replace the misleading note about a verb supposedly rendered 'confess' when the text actually says 'believe.' Add the printed future instruction at the introductory verb. Remove redundant note c after resolving the wording.

reviews.reason: The negative prefixes in the finding and grasping clauses must remain. P115 apparatus 32 supplies καταδιώκομεν, supporting active pursuit rather than the current passive 'we are driven away.' The closing noun supplied as ምኅባሪነ should not be silently equated with an ordinary habitation term; its exact transcription and companion/company versus dwelling interpretation remain held.
reviews.suggested_text: Bounded repair: “Now we long for a little respite, but do not find it; we pursue [it], but do not grasp [it]; light has passed from before us …”
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace the passive interpretation with a note on active pursuit and the supplied object. Attach the grasping note to that verb. Attach any discussion of the closing noun directly to that noun's English rendering; remove the unrelated previous-rendering note.

reviews.reason: P116 prints negative prefixes in the believing and praising clauses; the supplied source has misread these as affirmative-looking forms. The English negatives are therefore not an unsupported reversal of the printed text. Apparatus 5 expressly identifies the following bracketed clause as dittography, stronger and more specific than 'may reflect a variant.' The internal printed asterisk in the kingdom expression is not a raised apparatus numeral.
reviews.suggested_text: For before him we did not believe, and we did not praise the name of the Lord of Spirits, [and we did not praise our Lord,] and our hope was in the scepter of our kingdom and in our glory.
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace the duplicate a notes with one uniquely marked note attached to the bracketed clause: 'Charles identifies this bracketed clause as dittography.' Delete the affirmative previous-rendering alternative. Attach the scepter note to 'scepter.'
reviews.suggested_source_text: እስመ፡ በቅድሜሁ፡ *ኢአመነ፡ ወኢሰባሕነ፡ ለስሙ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መናፍስት፡ [ወኢሰባሕናሁ፡ ለእግዚእነ፡] ወተስፋነ፡ ኮነ፡ ዲበ፡ በትረ፡ መንግሥት*ነ፡ ወዲበ፡ ስብሐቲነ።

reviews.reason: The printed negatives support failure of rescue and absence of respite. The syntax does not securely establish the current English dependency 'no rest to believe that'; ንእመን may instead introduce a distinct acknowledgment. The printed sequence includes works, judgment, and righteousness, so note c's shortened alternative should not silently displace that sequence.
reviews.suggested_text: Bounded repair: “… he does not save us, and we find no respite. … Our Lord is faithful in all his works, his judgments, and his righteousness; his judgments show no partiality.” The connection of ንእመን remains held.
reviews.footnote_changes: Move the syntactic uncertainty note to ንእመን's English equivalent. Move the face-lifting idiom note to 'show no partiality.' Remove note c unless its omitted material is explicitly justified as a variant rather than ordinary translation.

reviews.reason: The condemned rulers remain the first-person speakers. Passing from his presence because of their deeds and judicial reckoning of their sins are supported. 'Counted in righteousness' needlessly risks suggesting that sins count as righteousness; 'reckoned justly' preserves the judicial sense.
reviews.suggested_text: And we shall pass from his presence[a] because of our deeds, and all our sins will be reckoned justly[b].
reviews.footnote_changes: Attach a to 'his presence' and b to 'reckoned justly.' Delete redundant note c. The present-versus-future English choice should not be presented as a manuscript variant.

reviews.reason: This remains the rulers' lament, not a newly identified divine speaker. The precise subject/object construction of the introductory verb should not be resolved solely by smoothing 'to them' into 'to themselves.' The negative preventing clause must remain. P116 apparatus 29 explicitly questions a burden/weight expression through the proposed βάρος/βάριν relationship and 'stronghold'; neither reading should be presented as unquestionably settled.
reviews.suggested_text: Bounded repair within the lament: “Our soul has had its fill of unjust gain, but it does not prevent our descent … into the burden of Sheol.” Hold the introductory addressee construction and the exact burden/stronghold wording.
reviews.footnote_changes: Attach the unjust-gain note to that phrase, the burden/stronghold discussion to 'burden,' and the Sheol note to 'Sheol.' Record that 'stronghold' is an editorially proposed explanation, not an unqualified translation of the supplied main-text spelling. Replace note d with an explicit account of the unresolved introductory construction.

reviews.reason: The royal quotation gives way to third-person narration. The opening printed verb is active; the current passive paraphrase conceals its implicit subject. Preserve that grammatical distinction without identifying an otherwise unstated agent. The subsequent expulsion and sword clauses should remain separate.
reviews.suggested_text: After this, he will fill their faces with darkness and shame before that Son of Man; they will be driven from his presence, and a sword will abide before his face in their midst.
reviews.footnote_changes: Explain at the opening verb that the grammatical subject is implicit and is not newly identified by this translation. Move the sword-construction note to the final clause and the Son of Man note to that title. Delete redundant note c.

reviews.reason: The current canonical source and English stop after the first addressee group. P116–117 continues with kings, the exalted, and those possessing the dry land, followed by 'before the Lord of Spirits'; LXIV begins only afterward. The supplied whole-unit candidate does not make the clipped canonical chapter complete. P116 apparatus 41–42 addresses the ordinance/judgment possessive constructions and explicitly flags unusual syntax. Do not silently choose singular versus plural possessives, resolve the addressee prepositions as exclusively for or against, or absorb the final 'before' phrase into one preferred construction.
reviews.suggested_text: Bounded repair: retain the introductory speech and restore all four groups—mighty ones, kings, exalted ones, and those possessing the dry land—together with the final 'before the Lord of Spirits.' Hold a continuous final translation until the ordinance/judgment possessives and prepositional attachments are explicitly represented.
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace a: ይቤ introduces speech; its presence does not justify suppressing that speech introduction. Expand b to distinguish the addressee preposition from the final 'before' phrase. Replace c with a precise discussion of p116 apparatus 41–42, distinguishing printed main text from possessive variants. Attach each note to its actual expression.
